commit.message:
Improve shaft self description

Mention that you can't use it on stairs or in water.

Add another word to Crazy Yiuf speech.

Taken from Mark Twain's "Extract from Captain Stormfield's Visit to
Heaven."

Remove redundant "the" in ghost descriptions.

Since the ghost's title should have whatever article is needed already.

Be more explicit about Fedhas plant move speed

It adds 5 aut to a normal speed move, so explicitly call it slow.

Show TRJ destruction for remembered walls

This makes autoexplore work better if the loot vaults had been seen, and
also just looks a bit cooler.

Tag a sealed area no_item_gen and no_monster_gen

Closes #5318.
Add pumpkincat to CREDITS.

Increase chance of Xom orb flavor text

The odds of Xom generating an orb are already quite low,
so an additional 25% chance of printing the unique flavor text
would seem excessive.

Remove unnecessary god_acting call

The function _xom_make_item calls god_acting to update global state,
but the only path by which this function is called goes through
xom_take_action, which already does this.

Fix unreachable Xom flavor text

The function _xom_make_item has unique flavor text for when Xom
gifts the player an orb.
Previously, this flavor text was only emitted when the arguments
to _xom_make_item specifically indicated an orb.
However, _xom_make_item is only ever called from one place,
with arguments of OBJ_RANDOM, so this flavor text was unreachable.
Fix this by inspecting the type of the object that is ultimately
generated, rather than the function arguments.

[Committer's notes: Don't set up the item_def used to inspect the
generated object until after the item is actually generated. The item
could be destroyed if you're over lava when Xom tries to gift it, in
which case inspecting it is useless.]
Fix typo in xom_event_data documentation

Don't claim two-handed weapons will be slowed by a shield (SammyHandelman)

Since you can't use both them and a shield at the same time.

Fix a bug with autopickup display on reload

When reloading the game, we drew the level before reading the init file.
This meant that map information which depends on the rc file didn't
load. This for exampe meant that redundant rings were displayed as
needing autopickup (this is true even with the default init file).

We fix this by doing an extra full draw after reading the init file. It
might be possible to fix it by instead moving the read of the init file
earlier, but this might mess up rc files which rely on the level being
loaded when they are run.

Adjust weights of new demon artefact brands.

The first four brands (chaos, draining, reaping, and vampirism) keep the
highest weights to bias these weapons toward chaos and evil, and
reaping's being more common on demonic artefact weapons thematically
fits. My justification for the others is as follows:

If we assume some of these demons are fighting each other with these,
thematically, antimagic cuts out the biggest advantage many demons have
against other demons (spells); distortion is more dangerous to its
wielders but sends other demons to the Abyss (where they will either be
killed or join Lugonu, become even stronger, and escape); and pain is
least common because it does nothing special to demons but aids demons
with necromancy against their living enemies.

Make demon weapon randart generation more interesting

Currently, demon weapon randarts have a 7/9 chance to generate with a
brand chosen from an unweighted list of mostly non-evil brands. Only 3
out of the 7 brands are actually evil-aligned, and there is about a 50%
chance for any given demon weapon randart to be flaming or freezing.
This commit changes demon weapon randart generation to only apply the
'special' brand override 1/3 of the time, but guarantees that the chosen
brand will be of an evil nature (or antimagic). This should make demon
weapon randart generation a little more thematic and varied.

Actually remove torment immunity from player plants (dilly)

2bbf0e9 only removed immunity from monster plants. Whoops.

Better-inform the player that ?tele is making the Abyssal rune more distant

By giving an additional message when reading ?tele in the Abyss without
having the rune, and also at the end of your teleport, when it pulls them
further away.

Hopefully this will reduce the number of people chain-reading ?tele and
being confused why they never find anything. >.>

Allow setting of base training targets

From the base tab of the skill menu, the player can now set a target for
base skill rather than modified skill. This is useful when e.g. setting
a target for shapeshifting to an amount where you intend to remove
wildshape.

If the skill is modified, targets are only shown on one menu, so that
players can easily distinguish between the two types of target.

Fixes #5029

Fix all cleaving attacks having a to-hit of 0 (dilly)

When 62da445 moved the point where to_hit is calculated, it accidentally
put it in a place that is skipped for cleaving attacks, resulting in them
almost always missing.

It's possible I should reconsider how this is organized, but this ought to
fix the immediate problem, at least.

Mention vampire form's passive daze in the talisman description

It should make the 'Daze Power' listed in the form table slightly less
mysterious to those who don't already know.

Apply Vainglory's conduct even while melded

To avoid people dipping stairs while, say, in medusa form.

(Vainglory's conduct is less severe than Toga of Victory's, but a similar
logic was already used there.)
Be a little more explicit about Hurl Torchlight giving undead energy

Fix redundant messages for eating invisible monsters in Maw form

Now that attacks against invisible monsters generally produce 'the
invisible X' instead of 'something', you would get redundant messages like
"You devour the invisible unseen horror. It tastes like unseen horror."
(What else would it taste like?)

It's a bit hard to actually eat a monster you're not aware of, since you'd
have to one-shot them while being unable to see them, but it's not
impossible...

List current banes in chardumps/morgues (Planckenstein)

I hadn't actually realized they weren't shown there anywhere, until now.
(The listing for mutations in dumps uses a separate codepath than the
mutation menu itself, these days.)

Fix monster Shatter being unaffected by Brilliance and Diminish Magic

(And being a Figment.)
Display monster Shatter damage on xv (Flugkiller)

Don't allow bound enemies to attack things while afraid (knorpule3001)

When 1ea72b2 improved attacking logic for bound enemies in some scenarios,
it also allowed them to ignore some other logic that would have prevented
them from attacking at all, like being afraid.

(Also, they shouldn't become more accurate at attacking the player while
confused or the player is invisible. If they guess the right spot, they'll
still be able to attack, but won't get, essentially, guided aim while
bound.)

Slightly clarify Mask of the Dragon's Dragonpray (confidence interval)

Don't imply that it doesn't work with gods whose skills scale off something
other than Invocations.
Fix werewolf form's howl affecting monsters through glass (canofworms)

Allow stokers to open doors (acrobat)

They're an intelligent, spellcasting skeleton (on the lich glyph, even!).
I'm sure they can figure out a doorknob.

Make player shadows created by Dith wrath a little scarier

They compared pretty poorly to the shadow puppet wrath option.

Attribute player shadows animated by Dith wrath to Dith

Being created in a non-standard way, they didn't get proper blame
attribution.

Remove is_follower()

There was only one use left and it could easily be more specific.

(Good riddance?)

Fix (non-Beogh) god summons not being dismissed on abandonment/penance

*Also* broken since 62137d7 (geeze, there's a lot of that, huh?) where
summoned allies stopped counting as followers for many gods. They didn't
even stop being friendly!

Funnily enough, I think the is_follower() call was redundant here if it
worked as originally intended, so I have just removed it.

(Also, dismiss summons via timeout instead of reset, so it actualy produces
messages and appropriate clouds.)

Don't try to make allies of good god worshippers have rHoly or rFoulFlame-

This hasn't actually done anything since 62137d7 but I don't feel
particularly inclined to put it back. It's a *very* marginal effect.

If we wanted a passive defensive buff to TSO allies, I think rN+++ would be
more interesting (and a lot more relevant).

Fix a convoluted moncast.lua test failure

Even in the test case where both test statues are allies of each other, the
test harness was setting the caster's foe to the other statue.

Allies should not normally be foes of each other, which was leading to an
assert via Grave Claw. Grave Claw's tracer merely checked that the caster
had a visible foe in range (since it can always hit them, if so). And they
did (since their ally was incorrectly set as their foe). But the spell
itself uses the default beam target for its aim, which setup_mons_cast()
*doesn't* set to the position of its foe (since it's not an enemy), leaving
the target at (0, 0).

Casting spells at (0, 0) is often safe, however Grave Claw does damage via
a beam that has a source equal to its target (just as Call Down Lightning
and many other smite-targeted effects do), and a *source* that is out of
boundns (ie: (0, 0)) asserts, causing the test to fail.

This mistake of setting allied foes has been true for moncast.lua possibly
since monsters could ever cast Grave Claw, so why didn't it happen before?
Well, you see, despite having an allied foe, Grave Claw always got vetoed
because the caster couldn't *see* their target since they'd made it
invisible via casting Invisibility Other at some point earlier in the test,
hiding this issue entirely. The crash only started happening now because
they *weren't* successfully making the other statue invisible.

Why weren't they? Because casting Invisibility on themselves was *moving*
them (as was just fixed by the previous commit) and sometimes, depending on
where they moved, a summon created by an earlier spell would now be in the
way of the Invisibility Other beam, preventing them from making their foe
invisible, thus allowing them to actually see them (incorrectly) as a valid
target for Grave Claw, thus crashing.

(This *still* should have been a possible fail state for almost 2 months
now. I can only assume that some unrelated change adjusted the RNG state
by the time it reached this point in the test suite, which allowed Invis to
move the statue in front of a summon when previously it did not.)

Anyway! Now we don't set the other statue as a foe unless they're hostile.

Don't shift immobile monsters after they cast Invisibility

It's not actually a translocation. (And even those shouldn't move literally
stationary monsters.)
Don't Daze the player while already Dazed (or stun-immune)
Remove a stray commented line

Don't make archer monsters spawn with their launcher unequipped

All equipment-using monsters prioritized starting with a melee weapon
equipped, regardless of whether they actually had one or not. This meant
that most archer enemies would spawn unarmed. This was especially
silly-looking for spells that summoned archers, who would arrive seemingly
without a weapon.

(This is the very tiniest of buff to archer monsters, since them wielding
their weapon upon spotting the player only took 2 aut. It's mostly a
visual improvement, for a couple spells in particular.)

Make the was_seen argument of change_monster_type() do something

While setting this to false technically suppressed the *immediated*
encounter message from polymorphing, it still made the monster count as
never seen, which would cause an encounter message to be printed slightly
later anyway.

If we set this to false, we probably want to *actually* suppress such, so
preserve the MF_SEEN flag in this case.

Tweak guardian mummy weapon offset, show shields

And also show weapons for royal mummies. The tile was clearly drawn with
weapon attachments in mind; it baffles me how it went these many years
without them being enabled.

Slightly refactor moving of dynamic map markers

A marginally more elegant solution than 3aa999a

Fix terrain changes that expire on monster death being slightly delayed

8b4cf4e had an oversight that caused the general 'remove linked terrain
changes on monster death' to not actually happen in many cases. But since
linked terrain changes automatically expire at the end of turn if their
source monster isn't alive, it usualy *looked* like it was happening
immediately.

This slight delay (ie: 'at end of turn' versus 'immediately after monster
death') is generally unlikely to have been consequential for most things
up to this point, but slightly incorrect. (And more noticable in
combination with some upcoming monster content.)

Fix the bonus accuracy from some attacks not working

Procs from Sundering and Rebuke brands, as well as attacks made by
stampeding monsters, were intended to have bonus accuracy, but because
to_hit was calculated by the attack's constructor, this bonus was never
seen.

This commit moves the calculation to handle_phase_attempted() instead
(which already made adjustments to to_hit in some cases, such as
AF_SHADOWSTAB), so that these bonuses work.

Revenant's spellclaw attacks while Enkindled were also intended to be
AUTOMATIC_HIT, but given that the species (and this ability) has proven
very powerful, I'm leaving the status quo alone. (And thus removing the
code which would do this, since it would now actually work.)

Remove some useless code

With a TODO that was already implemented elsewhere years ago!

Fix a handful of beam effects extending out of LoS

Beam range being capped to the player's LoS range was mostly done at the
level of spell_range() or ability_range() and beams themselves would
happily accept longer ranges than this. This resulted in a handful of
things that were neither spells nor direct abilities having range 8
regardless of the player's LoS (since they were setting bolt.range
manually).

This included the beams from Vitriol and Pain cards (which extended
slightly out of LoS on everyone but barachi and *very far* out of sight on
kobolds). It also affected beams from valour-branded weapons if your LoS
was small enough (kobold + some LoS reducer), which could even be a
practical and repeatable benefit.

(It also affected a number tracers, such as for salvo targeting, which may
possibly have caused an effect to think it could hit something even if it
could not - the actual shot itself had its range properly capped.)

Beams now automatically cap their range at you.current_vision. (In
reviewing existing uses, I didn't notice any places that might rely on
being able to fire out of sight and am not sure what such a thing might
even be.)

bolt::range now also defaults to LOS_RADIUS instead of -2 (which would
assert if not manually specified in every single case) allowing a bunch of
simple effects to skip defining it. (It feels like a sensible default to
me and saves a line in the common case that you're already aiming at a
specific destination.)

Fix a missing break

If the player had sticky flame while also being able to currently join
Beogh, the sticky flame light would also say Beogh.

Beogh Beogh.

Allow dismissing/recruiting apostles while silenced

This feels more like bookkeeping than it does invoking a god's powers (and
has the chance to cause an unexpected feelsbad situation when defeating an
apostle while silenced and being unable to recruit them).

(Also allow you to name your ancestor while silenced, which feels even more
UI-related.)

Don't hide (many) god abilities while silenced

While most god abilities cannot be used while silenced, we were somewhat
inconsistent about whether we hid the ability entirely or merely greyed it
out - largely as a consequence of code ordering in get_god_abilities().
For instance, the abilities to choose an ancestor type would be visible
while silenced (but still unusuable) while other Hep abilities would be
hidden. Ru sacrifice abilities were visible, but other Ru abilities hidden.

But in general, it feels odd to me to hide abilities that the player still
has for such a transient effect as silence - potentially even confusing to
players. So now, we should no longer hide any of them.

(This should not affect whether they're actually usuable or not.)

Look up ability definitions via map instead of linear search

Probably inconsequential, but feels more appropriate when we're regularly
doing lookups in a 160+ entry array.

Give Cleansing Flame an actual message when the player uses it

And move the additional message printed when a monster casts it into
monspell.txt so that they don't need to additionally gesture first.

Make Cleansing Flame ignore all allies

Prior to 62137d7 accidentally breaking it, it was *effectively* harmless to
most of the player's allies, since they were given immunity to holy energy,
but instead let's just make it only hit enemies. (This is a lot less spammy
of messages, too).

Make Summon Holy Warrior's duration a bit more consistent

The average duration of the summoned creatures was quite large, but the
formula involved was kind of odd and allowed extremely low-rolling the
duration sometimes (for instance, the average duration at 12 evo was 130
turns, but it was possible to roll as low as 8 turns!)

This makes the low-end a lot less low while keeping the average fairly
similar to before.

Replacement for TSO's ally blessing effects.

This replacement has two aspects:

1) Allies who are fighting evil creatures will not have their summon timers
   decrease.

This is a replacement for the old duration increasing blessing and is more
reliable, but also can't stack immense durations of extra time when out of
combat. It is, however, significantly more powerful for short-duration
non-holy summons, which received a much weaker effect from the old
blessing. Summon Hydra users rejoice!

2) Whenever the player kills a monster directly, there is a chance for TSO
to bless a random ally with either a burst of instant energy (equivalent to
3 turns) or a temporary divine shield.

This is a replacement for the old healing blessing (exchanging healing with
reliable protection to further differentiate it from Ely's increased
ability to heal the player's allies now).

Only allies who are already injured will be given a divine shield (to
increase the chance that it actually does something, since many allies may
not actually be under fire at any given time, especially if the player is
leading from the front).

Unlike the old blessings, this doesn't work when allies score the kills
themselves (to encourage the player to *lead* their army), but also no
longer requires that the monster killed be evil. TSO in past was sometimes
talked about as a possible summoner support god, but limiting their ally
benefits to evil creatures was fairly narrow. They are already better
against evil monsters in so many ways that I think it's fine if this
is more general).

The chance may be somewhat generous, but given the stipulations involved,
I didn't want it to feel overly marginal, either. Let's see how it feels.

Implement a Divine Shield status for monsters

This works pretty much exactly the like the player TSO ability, providing
a small number of charges of automatic blocking, along with reflection and
retaliatory blinding in melee.

Intended to be used as part of a TSO ally-buffing effect, but also may have
future possibilities for a TSO-themed unique.

(Divine Shield status icon made by regret-index, modifying ontoclasm's edit
of Grunt's Injury Mirror status icon.)

Let +SH artprops items work on monsters

This is currently only the Brooch of Shielding and one of the Rings of the
Octopus King, but an oversight nonetheless.

Remove actor::shielded()

This was used to determine whether to perform a block check for beams
fired at the player (and orbs of destruction fired at anyone) and was not
only superfluous with checking whether the defender actually had any SH,
but practically begging to go out of sync with it. Which it (very slightly)
already had: the SH bonus from rebuke weapons in monster hands didn't
apply to iood hits.

Instead, just check SH directly (which is what most other places already
did).

Remove vestigial TSO follower blessings, pending rework

TSO follower blessings were broken completely almost two years ago (as a
result of a small error in 62137d7 which caused all summoned allies to be
ineligible for them). I am surprised nobody noticed in this time, but the
duration extension one is fairly consequential.

However, several parts of this blessing system were super marginal and/or
broken for even longer (for example, I think the duration extension for
charmed enemies hasn't functioned since 0e8e6b5) and I've wanted to rewrite
this in past. So I'm using this as a chance for a clean break, and will
be replacing it with entirely new code.

Allow Ely's Divine Vigour to affect allies as well (regret-index)

In the continuing theme of improving Ely's ability to actually support
othes, Divine Vigour has been renamed Aura of Vigour and now provides the
Doubled Vigour buff to all nearby friendly creatures for as long as the
effect is active on the player.

(There's an amusing cycle to the Apis aura being originally inspired by
Divine Vigour and now in turn changing Divine Vigour itself to be more like
the apis aura.)

While this is another flat Ely buff, it is again only a buff to 'summoner
of Ely', which is not exactly a popular archetype at present, so I think
it should be okay.

-----------------

The new Aura of Vigour ability icon was made by regret-index, using the
previous Divine Vigour invocation icon.

Refactor monster aura handling a little

In preparation for auras that come from things other than monsters.

Split Ely's Heal Other into Pacify and Divine Alms

While Heal Other could, in theory, be used for the purposes of healing
an ally, in practice it was almost impossible to justify spending that
piety to mildly heal someone (who you could usually have just resummoned at
full HP whenever you wanted) instead of using it to instantly remove an
enemy. In fact, so strong is the assumption that you'll use Heal Other to
pacify things that even when aimed at an ally, it reports your chance to
pacify them. I mean, why would you be using it on something that wasn't
hostile?

But it seems a shame that those worshipping The Healer can't justify
actually healing anyone who is injured (besides themselves). Summoner of
Ely builds are already a bit niche, and the incentive to heal summons is
low, so I think we can try being a lot more generous here if we want to
capture any of the flavor of actually being a healer.

Given the two 'modes' of Heal Other really want very different levels of
power, this commit splits it in two:

Pacify takes on most of the current role of Heal Other, but more
explicitly. It can only be aimed at hostile targets, but otherwise
functions almost identically to how Heal Other does now, with two small
changes:
 -Instead of an invo-based random heal applied to the monster only if the
  pacification succeeds, it now just heals them to full in that case
  instead.
 -Player ghosts and random Pan lords are no longer immune to it.
  (b5b494a did this on account of Pan lord HP being highly randomised, but
  hidden. However, xv has shown their exact HP since dc84959 so I think
  there's no longer any need for this).

Its code has also been heavily refactored to use a proper targeter,
slightly improving its UI.

Divine Alms is the part that actually wants to heal allies. It heals for a
larger amount, removes the same status effects that Purification does from
the player, and also gives a small amount of additional duration to any
summons it heals (to keep the heal from potentially being entirely wasted
on them). It also costs NO piety. (I considered making it instead cost
'the smallest possible amount', but even then I feel players would hesitate
to use it over other way to spend piety, which undercuts some of the point
of it existing at all.)

Note: it can only be used on *friendly* monsters, specifically to avoid the
almost guaranteed result of the best targets for it otherwise being 'a
pacified monster that is currently massacring its former allies for you.'
It's already enough flavor clash for that to be an important aspect of
pacification targeting; I don't want to emphasise it further.

In any case, while this is strictly a buff to a god that is already
reasonably powerful, it is also a buff only to a much less common
play-pattern and one that seems very congruent with Ely's theoretical
flavour. Let's see how it feels.

-------------------------

The new Pacify and Divine Alms icons were made by regret-index,
combining ontoclasm's current Elyvilon ability icons along with his
donation to Zin icon and a CC0 dove by Clint Bellanger.

Allow allied plants to fire through Fedhas-worshipping players (if a plant)

Fedhas-made plants have always been able to fire through other plant
*monsters* (just as the player can), but not through the player if *they*
were a plant. Which was always possible with !lig and considerably more
possible now that vine stalkers are also plants.

It seems a harmless niche benefit to me.
Describe the benefits of being a plant on the mutation screen

Make vine stalkers into actual plants

Despite being very plant-themed, vine stalkers weren't actually plants in
any mechanical sense (perhaps due to wanting to avoid making them torment
immune?) Some of the thematic justification for this was that the vines are
growing out of a still-not-quite-dead animal (which was being parasitised).
But the manual has long described them as absent of any discrenable
features besides their maws, suggesting they've never been using the
original host's eyes or ears or any other part that should tie them
inexorably to animal biology.

(Which is a long way of saying: why *not* be a real plant now?)

This comes with a few minor benefits, such as unbreathing and immunity to
sleep. Which is a small buff to the species, but I think not a significant
one.

(Also, Maurice is now peaceful to Fedhas-worshippers.)

Be more explicit about what being undead / 'nonliving' does for players

Include a longer fakemut, with description, on the A screen whenever the
player is fully undead or whatever passes for nonliving as a player -
enumerating the majority of the innate properties of being such, especially
those not mentioned elsewhere.

Make all stationary plants will-immune, boost will of several others

Partially in compensation for no longer being immune to fear, oklob plants
and several other stationary 'non-sentient' plants are now will-immune
(I'll be honest, until recently, I thought they already were - possibly due
to them being immune to multiple hexes anyway). And the willpower of
several high-tier mobile plant monsters is increased somewhat.

Allow plant monsters to berserk and feel fear

In retrospect, it's a little silly that plants were immune to fear when we
had plants who were defined around the idea of 'being really nervous all of
the time'.

Tweak a few monster resists

Creeping Infernos and Lurking Horrors are now will-immune (which is very
common for 'projectile-like' enemies).

Rusted Inspectors are also will-immune and no longer human intelligence
(to be more consistent with golems in general).

Will-o-the-wisps are now fire-immune (considering they are literally made
of the stuff, this seems reasonable).

Make a couple things no longer check holiness directly

Status darts now check rPois-immunity instead of 'not undead or nonliving'
which is *almost* the same thing (but allows Staff of Olgreb and
Vitalisation to protect the player).

Deathly Blight (from death form) now checks rN immunity for its draining
effect and demonspawn weakness stinger checks rPois-immunity, for an even
less impactful change.

Fix some monster cast logic that still thought plants had rN+++

Monsters would not consider using Vampiric Draining, Draining Gaze,
March of Sorrows, Mourning Wail, Bolt of Draining, Malign Offering, or
Ghostly Fireball if their primary foe was a plant (despite most of them
having no rN)

Don't limit Scythe of Curses to cursing living/plant enemies

It's unclear why it had this limitation given that regular mummy death
curses work even on the undead just fine. (The in-game description was also
arguably misleading, since it did work on plants.)

Take away gargoyle/djinni immunity to draining weapons

This was a little odd, since many nonliving player forms don't even have
rN (and gargoyles only have rN+). But despite most sources of negative
energy damage working on them, draining brand and AF_DRAINING never would.

Now these check rN only.

Fix monster Cause Fear not working on demons and holies

When 070a2a6 allowed demons and holies to be feared, the monster version of
this spell didn't get the memo.

Take away 'nonliving' players' fear immunity

It wasn't commonly known that gargoyles and djinni were fear-immune in the
first place (even the wiki doesn't mention it) and while nonliving monsters
*are* immune, they also can't berserk. Whatever the player is clearly has
enough emotions to get pissed off, so I think they also have enough
emotions to be afraid.

(This will have some further relevance in the upcoming Tomb rework.)

Make plants torment-vulnerable, buff tree form

When rN+++ was taken away from plants by 662dcd3 it was noted that it made
sense that pain-flavored effects wouldn't work on plants, but in fact many
pain-flavored effects *do* work on plants (including the spell Pain and
Pain-branded weapons and Anguish, to list a few).

Following the prior commit to treat plants as closer to living beings, this
removes their general torment resistance. However, since torment immunity
is a cute use case for !lignification in the lategame that feels good to
preserve, I am instead making it a special property of the specific tree
you turn into - and at the same time, giving it back the rN+++ that it lost
at the same time (which I think is also somewhat cute as it covers the hole
that !resistance has).

(This also allows future plant forms without being forced to give them all
torment-immunity, which is mechanically problematic.)

-----------------------------

The new banyan tree tile was made by regret-index, combining ontoclasm's
current tree form tile with Sastreii's dead tree and demonic tree tiles.

Allow derived undead made from plants

The game often refers to effects working on 'living' monsters, by which
what we really tend to mean are 'animals', but plants are by all reasonable
definitions alive. And in fact, 'undead plants' have been in DCSS as
monsters since the very beginning. So I don't see any particular reason
why it's inappropriate that you can raise zombies from plants, either.

(Whether or not a thorn hunter is sapient enough to have a soul which can
stand outside its body is a theological question for which I think a
reasonable answer is "If a slime mold has one, this can too.")

------------------------

The new fungus and tree derived undead tiles were made by regret-index,
using the following pieces:

 * Zombie / spectral fungi: Sastreii's sleepcap tile, ontoclasm's edit of
   Denzi's wandering mushroom tile, and previously-rejected tree tiles
   made by roctavian.
 * Zombie plants: Roctavian's thorn hunter tile and CC0 tufts of grass
   by pixel-boy.
 * Zombie trees: Purge's old dead tree tile, one of Sastreii's demonic tree
   tiles, and CanOfWorms's old flying skull tile.
 * Fungus simulacra: Ontoclasm's large humanoid, small humanoid, and naga
   simulacra tiles.
 * Tree simulacra: Ontoclasm's snake, spider, and large humanoid simulacra

Give player gargoyles / djinni souls

'Nonliving' players have never really played by the same rules as nonliving
monsters. They lack many iconic immunities nonliving monsters have (eg:
negative energy, torment, mutation, polymorph, and berserk) and while many
of those may be for mechanical reasons *first*, I think it necessarily
implies that you are far more 'alive' than a random statue - you just lack
fleshy biology.

Given that fleshy players can freely shift in and out of non-fleshy forms
via talismans (eg: living scroll, statue, and storm), it feels reasonable
to interpret this as 'the real you' still being down there somewhere,
beneath this transformation. (After all, you can still mutate changes to
your arms and legs while being a vaguely person-shaped thunderhead.)

As such, I think it reasonable to say that gargoyles and djinni also have
a soul. (As part of a project to fix a handful of possible inconsistencies
with player nonliving resists and make what resists they *do* have more
explicit in the interface).

(In practice, all this specific commit does is make you succeptible to
Soul Splinter and Umbral Torchlight.)

Group many natural/holy/demonic checks into actor::has_soul()

Representing a common class of 'resist' rather than bespoke holiness checks
every time. (In anticipation of an upcoming change to the player's end of
this.)

Don't give the player nonliving holiness while petrified

This was fairly obscure, hard to look up (you can't check % while
petrified!) and unlikely to be relevant. Moreover, it had a couple
oddities:
 -Undead players stopped being undead while petrified, meaning they could
  no longer be affected by Dispel Undead, Dominate Undead, or Undeadhunter
  (though holy wrath weapons still worked, since they *don't* use a
  holiness check).
  -This could also give the wrong god message if you died that way
 -Monsters never behaved this way (as is very obvious with, say, poison
  continuing to damage them).
 -The fact that petrification works on undead, who are otherwise immune to
  polymorph and form changes, suggests something else is happening anyway.

I considered going the other direction and making it work more fully for
players and monsters, but giving a handful of immunities to petrified
monsters feels like an unnecessary nerf to a comparatively unpopular spell
and makes medusa form have wild antisynergy with itself (ie: you only
petrify monsters who are poisoned, but then they stop being affected by
that poison...)

Rework a number of vampirism checks (generally in monsters' favour)

actor_is_susceptible_to_vampirism() was used to control whether an actor
could heal from a given target (ie: to prevent the player from healing via
Vampiric Draining summons), but also excluded several other categories of
creature and was used to determine whether creatures could be damaged by
effects like Drain Life.

Significantly, since 36912a8 player gargoyles and djinni (and storm form,
etc.) became completely immune to Drain Life, despite several of those not
even getting a single pip of natural rN. d5a6684 had a similar effect on
Vampiric Draining.

On top of this, it's honestly very silly to have a monster AoE spell that
mostly could only affect the player (since your allies almost always count
as summoned and are immune). The 'no summons' stipulation is really very
player-gameplay-centric, which is somewhere I think it's fine to be
asymmetric.

This commit makes the following changes:

-The holiness check is replaced entirely with the pre-existing rN check
 (which removes player djinni/gargoyle's unexpected immunity, but generally
 does not affect monsters)
-Monsters can now freely use all vampirism effects against summoned
 monsters and heal from it (a minor and reasonable summoner nerf in a
 handful of places)
-Even the player can now *damage* summons via Vampiric Draining (though
 they still cannot heal from them).

(For reference, Fathomless Shackles already had the behavior of 'can damage
summons, but not gain life from them' and Malign Offering worked fully on
summons and player gargoyles already.)

Remove monster memories when we see them again

This removes remembered information about a monster when they are in
view again, or leave a level.

The motivation is just that it's a bit ugly to have loads of copies of a
monster remembered, especially when e.g. permanent allies are following
a player at the edge of their LoS.

This gives the player slightly more info than before - they can know
that monsters are the same ones they've seen before. This information is
only very weakly hidden already, as encounter messages give a lot of it,
and it seems fine to consider it not a secret.

Codewise, we do this by having monsters know where they were last seen,
so that when they are seen again they can wipe that memory.

mode function, prevent this from happening in that one case.

Tag a wall mimic vault as no_tele_into (mat4rat4s)

It is technically possible to teleport into darby_miner_ambush without
having ever approached it from the outside (thus revealing the wall mimcs).
Unlike other occluding-terrain mimic vaults, such as Rutra's trove or
darby_rabbit_hole, it would also impugn on the flavour and mechanics of
such a hostile vault to provide repeated escape hatches out from it.
As such, I am tagging the vault as no_tele_into instead, to preserve the
intended approach towards the vault rather than removing it entirely.

(For the most part, terrain mimic vaults should remain rare, though the
addition of earlygame vaults using such in e.g. b49e76e and 0383675 has
reasonably increased this count. I would rather not remove such vaults
entirely or push such to depths where players will plausibly always have
spare teleport scrolls: early mimic vaults are good tutorialization for
other notable uses of mimics like the rune mimics, and the terminally
incurious will suffer plenty from not wanting to learn in this comically
maximalist game's opposition. If any other wall / liquid mimic vaults come
up in the future that don't elicit using various hatches, they should also
just use no_tele_into props.)
